messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED  CRITICAL: CorvusCorp (enterprise, eu-central) persistent 5xx + connection resets on dedicated pool (dp-corvus-euc1). Paging oncall: liam-sre. :rotating_light:
liam-sre: I'm oncall. seeing ~22% 5xx, lots of connection resets, p95 latency up. Topology: dp-corvus-euc1 (3xA40) serving CorvusCorp via dedicated tenant mapping.
network-bot: observed burst of TCP RSTs from node gpu-12; dmesg shows GPU driver recoveries around same time.
liam-sre: suspect GPU driver stalls causing health probe failures and reconnections. spawning investigation. @sarah-csm can you ping the customer and ask them to hold non-critical batch jobs? they were running nightly bulk jobs earlier.
sarah-csm: on it. told Corvus to pause bulk loads and that we're investigating. They asked if we'll failover them  they have strict IP allowlists on their firewall, so cross-region cutover will need update.
liam-sre: immediate mitigations: 1) try warm-pool attach in same region (dp-corvus-euc1-warm) 2) if attach fails/incompatible drivers, plan B: cross-region reroute to dp-corvus-euw1-warm and coordinate customer firewall whitelist for temporary IPs; 3) DNS CNAME cutover as last resort (TTL ~60s but client caching still an issue).
nora-platform: initiating warm attach (same-region) now.
deploy-bot: job attach-warm/1766666000 started -> job-id: attach-7741
nora-platform: attach FAILED: control-plane reports node driver mismatch on warm pool (driver v470 vs v495). Can't attach due to incompatible ABI. :frowning: 
liam-sre: ok plan B. preparing cross-region reroute. @sarah-csm need customer approval to add ~8 egress IPs for 1 hour. Can you get that asap?
sarah-csm: Customer asked for list of IPs and confirmation of duration. I'm sending emergency allowlist email now and asked for ATO window (30-60m).
network-bot: candidate IPs for dp-corvus-euw1-warm: ["34.199.12.8","34.199.12.9","34.199.12.10","34.199.12.11","34.199.12.12","34.199.12.13","34.199.12.14","34.199.12.15"] (ops note: ephemeral pool NATs)
liam-sre: thanks. while we wait, rate-limit incoming batch requests for Corvus to reduce pressure. Applying request throttling policy now.
ops-bot: ROUTING UPDATE: creating rollout corvus-euc1-emergency (canary=0% -> will flip to 100% cross-region when CO returns OK)
nora-platform: ready to flip when customer confirms whitelist. preparing DNS fallback snippet:
```
# DNS provider update (example)
curl -X PATCH "https://dns-provider/api/zones/corvus.example/records/CNAME" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DNS_TOKEN" \n  -d '{"content":"cname.dp-corvus-euw1-warm.redwood.net","ttl":60}'
```
sarah-csm: Customer replied: "we can add temporary allowlist now for 45m". They added IPs and confirmed.
liam-sre: starting routing flip to dp-corvus-euw1-warm. will do a 25% -> 75% -> 100% ramp every 2m. watch 5xx and conn resets.
ops-bot: ROUTING UPDATE: rollout corvus-euc1-emergency -> 25% -> IN_PROGRESS
liam-sre: 25% done. initial metrics look improved, 5xx down to 6% on the target pool.
liam-sre: 75% now. p95 latency steady. conn resets largely gone for new connections.
ops-bot: ROUTING UPDATE: rollout corvus-euc1-emergency -> 75% -> IN_PROGRESS
liam-sre: 100% flip completed. ROUTING UPDATE: SUCCESS. traffic now on dp-corvus-euw1-warm.
sarah-csm: customer reports errors dropped to near zero. they asked how long until original region is safe.
liam-sre: we'll keep traffic on eu-west for 4h, during which platform + infra will reprovision dp-corvus-euc1 with updated driver and forced pod restarts. scheduling maintenance now.
nora-platform: reprovision job started: reprovision-dp-corvus-euc1 (job-id: repro-2229). will update driver to v495 matching warm pool.
deploy-bot: reprovision-dp-corvus-euc1 logs: https://ci.redwood/repro-2229
liam-sre: handing off to @nora-platform for remaining ops. I'm going offline for 30m, will join postmortem. :wave: 
nora-platform: acknowledged, taking over incident lead.
ops-bot: NOTE: added incident label "customer-allowlist-required" and created follow-up ticket P-9876 for driver upgrade audit.
liam-sre: INCIDENT MITIGATED  traffic shifted cross-region after customer allowlist, errors resolved. SLA exposure avoided. Post-incident actions: - permanent driver version pinning for dedicated pools - add preflight check for warm pool driver compatibility - docs update for customer firewall requirements during emergency cross-region failover. Scheduling 1h postmortem tomorrow 09:00 UTC with platform + infra + CSM.
sarah-csm: will loop in customer for RCA and timeline. they appreciated the rapid mitigation.
liam-sre: closing thread here. final status: RESOLVED. :white_check_mark:
